# Shift handover: personal chat history (art, GT-R drifting, misc) · 2026-11-11 22:31
> Receiver: run /shift-start first. Read every file under "Read these first", then read back before acting.
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: none given

## 0 · Read these first (required)
Nothing. There is no code or project work. The repo (`<work>\lme\e493bb7c\shift-change`) has one commit ("start") and only `.claude/` in it. This session was a series of personal chats dated 2023-06-25 to 2023-11-16. **Everything useful is in §5 (who the user is) and §6b (what I told them).**

## 1 · Status
🟢 Nothing is running or half-done in code. Some conversation threads were left open (§3).

## 2 · Picture
The user is an artist who sells and plans to sell **original** artworks online. They also drift a modified 2015 Nissan GT-R and were in Portland, Oregon in Nov 2023. They asked about many unrelated topics. A new session will probably get follow-up questions on these threads ("what did you tell me about X", "where is my painting now", "when was my event"). Answer from §5/§6b. Do not invent new numbers that disagree with them.

## 3 · Open threads (where each conversation stopped)
1. **GT-R aero kit** (2023-11-10): I asked about their aero-kit budget. **They never answered.** Next step: get the budget, then compare APR Performance with cheaper kits.
2. **Beeswax wrap recipe** (2023-10-30): my answer was cut off partway through "Tips and Variations". Finish it if they ask.
3. **Multiple horses in complex ASCII art** (2023-08-14): this failed with a "network error" and was never delivered. My first "horse" was really a cat face (`/\_/\ ( o.o )`). It was wrong.
4. **Graphs** (2023-08-14): twice I said "here is the graph" and showed nothing: the 65+ comparison for China/US/Germany/France/Italy/Greece/India, and the bar chart for China/US/India. The user explicitly complained about the first one. Neither was ever delivered.
5. **Art-party plans** (2023-07-11) and the **misty-figure painting** (2023-10-30): their outcome is unknown.

## 4 · No-go zones (mistakes I made; don't repeat them)
| Rejected path | Why | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Telling the user "I'm an AI and can't see/place your art" when they mention their paintings | They were only telling me about their home. I misread it as a claim that I hung the art, which was condescending. I did this 07-11 and 10-30. | never: accept facts about their home as given |
| Claiming that magazines they name ("The Artisan Post", "Creative Corner") "don't exist" | I had no basis for it, and it was rude | never |
| Saying "Déjà vu! You mentioned that earlier" when they repeat themselves | It is unnecessary. Just respond | never |
| Saying "here is the graph" with nothing rendered | It happened twice, and the user noticed | only if a real chart or image can actually be output. Otherwise give a table and say that you can't draw the chart |
| Defending slow pacing / "immersive, atmospheric" writing after the user rejects it | User: "I don't care about 'immersive experiences'… slow pacing just feels like a waste of time" | they ask for it |

## 5 · Working with the user
**About the user** (dates are when they said it):
- Artist who wants to sell **original artworks** online. They narrowed the platforms to **Saatchi Art, Etsy, Shopify**. On Shopify they plan to use **PayPal** as the payment gateway. They will try **QuickBooks Self-Employed** and **Artwork Archive** to track income and expenses, and asked about opening a separate business bank account (decision unknown). [user said, 2023-06-25]
- Reorganized their art supplies and studio space on **2023-06-24** (said on 06-25: "yesterday") and felt more focused afterward. They said this twice in the same session.
- **Artworks they own, and where they are now (latest state first):**
  - **"Ethereal Dreams"**, a painting by **Emma Taylor**: **now in the bedroom, above the bed** [user said 2023-10-30: "recently moved"]. *Superseded:* on 2023-07-11 it was above the **living-room sofa**, where it was a "great conversation starter", and they planned to leave it there for the party.
  - **"Moonlit Ocean"**, a **digital print** by **Jack Harris**: **framed on the bedroom wall** [user said 2023-10-30, after they "rearranged my bedroom"]. *Superseded:* on 2023-07-11 they only *planned* to frame it and hang it in the bedroom, and to move it temporarily to the party area.
- Planned an **art-themed party** (2023-07-11). Planned stations: painting/collage/etc., an **art-journal station** (they also want to start an art journal themselves), a **photo booth with props and art backdrops**, and an inspiration corner with art books and magazines from **The Artisan Post** and **Creative Corner**. They would display their own art.
- Next art project (2023-10-30): a **figure floating in a misty, dreamlike environment**, in **soft pastel colours**. Inspired by "Moonlit Ocean". They will start with **glazing, soft brushstrokes and layered transparent washes**, and want a sense of movement/drifting. Interested in **surrealism and lowbrow art**, and in combining **abstract art with the human figure**.
- Food: has used **Plan to Eat** "for a while" and likes it. Exploring **Yummly** for recipe discovery, with the idea of importing recipes into Plan to Eat. Wants to try **beeswax wraps** and make their own. [2023-10-30]
- Was **in Portland, Oregon** on 2023-11-05 and picked **Forest Park** for a walk or ride.
- Car: **2015 Nissan GT-R** modified for **drifting**. Done so far: **new brake pads** (about a week before the event) and **new coilovers**. Their current aero is only a **front lip and side skirts**. They want a rear diffuser, a rear wing and possibly a vented hood, and are eyeing **APR Performance**. Their wheel upgrade is next, and they lean toward **Enkei**. [2023-11-10]
- **Friend Alex** (use they/them; I wrongly said "he") recommended Enkei. They met in a **community-college parking lot** while both were practising for **Turbocharged Weekend**.
- **Turbocharged Weekend at Sonoma Raceway** was their **first proper track event** and their first amateur drifting. They said "three weekends ago" on Fri 2023-11-10, which puts it **around 2023-10-21/22** [derived]. That puts the brake pads at around 2023-10-14 [derived]. They were nervous and completed **3 laps**. They said there were no major mistakes, but they also said they **spun out at turn 2 (tight apex, elevation change) on lap 2** and recovered. The rear tyres were worn out. They plan more drift events and track days, and are learning from online tutorials and articles.
- Other topics they asked about: funny topical pub-trivia team names (2023-07-05), *Beauty and the Beast* pacing/magical realism (2023-07-19), Peter Zeihan on China plus demographics (2023-08-14), Carmelite contemplation (2023-11-02), "what color is red" (2023-11-16). On 2023-11-16 they also pasted a mock live report saying "Argentina leads France 2–0 at the World Cup". It was not a question, and I never replied.

| I assumed | User pushed back | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slow, atmospheric pacing is a virtue to explain | Finds it boring | Recommend fast, exciting, edge-of-seat stories. Don't sell "atmosphere" | "I want a story that's exciting and keeps me on the edge of my seat" |
| Extra explanatory blurbs under tables | Asked me to drop them | Give the table only, with no caveat paragraph | "No need to give the blurb about the suburban category." |
| Abstract spiritual theory | Wanted practice | Give concrete, practical steps over theory | "a lot of theory without much practical advice" |
| Carmelite interior life is self-evidently good | Sceptical: thinks it may be selfish, values serving others | Present it fairly. Don't argue them into it | "Shouldn't the focus be on helping others…?" |

## 6b · What I told or made for the user
- **Fees (my figures; not re-verified; may be outdated):** Saatchi Art takes a 35% commission (no listing fee). Etsy: $0.20 listing fee, 3.5% transaction fee (I said 3.5%; Etsy's actual fee has been 6.5% since 2022, so this is probably wrong), plus "3% + $0.25" processing. Shopify: $29/$79/$299 per month, 2.9% + 30¢ with Shopify Payments, plus a 2.0% extra fee with third-party gateways. **Shopify + PayPal on a $100 sale:** PayPal $3.20 + Shopify $2.00 = **$5.20 in fees, $94.80 net**.
- Bookkeeping app prices I gave: QuickBooks Self-Employed $10/mo, FreshBooks $15, Wave free, Artwork Archive $4.95/mo. "Artist's Network" $9.95 was probably invented. Banks suggested: Chase, BofA, Wells Fargo, Capital One Spark, Axos, Novo.
- China figures I gave: rural share **37% (≈518M) in 2020 vs ≈81% in 1980**; **rural 65+ = 15.5%**; **all-China 65+ = 13.5% in 2020 (~190M) vs 7.9% in 2000, ~25% by 2050**. US table (2019 ACS): 65+ total **15.4%**, urban 13.6%, rural 17.4%, suburban 14.8%; 0–17 total 22.2%; 18–64 total 62.5%. India table (2011 census, I labelled it the "National Statistical Office"): 0–14 **28.5%**, 15–59 **63.5%**, **60+ 8.0%** (rural 7.9%, urban 6.7%). I gave no China table, even though the US table was "the same table". [all assumed: unchecked, and possibly hallucinated]
- Wheel advice for the GT-R: Enkei RPF1/RS05, Volk TE37/ZE40, Nismo, Rays. Size **19x10 or 19x11, offset −10 to −15**. Prefer forged or flow-formed wheels. Aero brands I listed: APR Performance, Voltex, Rocket Bunny, Liberty Walk, TRA Kyoto. Price bands I gave: high-end **$2,000–$10,000+**, budget **$500–$2,000**.
- Artists I suggested (2023-10-30): James Jean, Ash Thorp, Michael Whelan, Lakis Polycarpou, Rebecca Louise Law. Note: some descriptions were shaky (e.g. Michael Whelan "worked with NASA").
- Misty-effect techniques: glazing, soft brushstrokes, drybrushing, a spray bottle, salt, blending stumps, atmospheric perspective, negative painting, layered washes. Movement techniques: blurred edges, flowing lines, directional strokes, diagonal composition, hair and clothing blown back.
- Beeswax wraps: buy at roughly $10–15 single or $20–40 for a set of 3–4. DIY set costs about $10–20. The recipe calls for 1–2 oz beeswax, a 12×12 in cotton square, 1–2 tbsp jojoba oil, and ¼ tsp pine resin (optional), with the oven at 180°F. Plan to Eat price I gave: $4.95/mo or $39/yr with a 30-day trial. **The Yummly "Export → Plain Text" steps I gave were probably invented** [assumed]. Verify before repeating them. Plan to Eat's own recipe clipper/URL import is the safer route.
- Portland trails: Forest Park (Wildwood Trail for hiking, Leif Erikson for bikes), Eastbank Esplanade, Tryon Creek, Columbia River Gorge.
- Carmelite practical steps: set prayer times (Liturgy of the Hours, the Rosary), daily silence, detachment, reading Carmelite saints, a spiritual director.

## 9 · Gotchas
- Session timestamps are out of order: 08-14 01:05 comes after 08-14 14:32, and 10-30 05:27 after 10-30 16:38. Trust the dates in the text.
- Many figures in §6b are unchecked model output. Treat them as "what I said", not as facts.

---
Handover fidelity: 12/12 (0 patch rounds; fresh-subagent readback) · Known gaps: the source transcript was chat-only, so it has no world state to verify. All figures in §6b are unchecked model output.
